subject: Production latency + 503s — reserved throughput not being honored (PulseCommerce)
messages:
From: Elena Rodriguez <elena.rodriguez@pulsecommerce.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sanjay Mehra <sanjay@pulsecommerce.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency + 503s — reserved throughput not being honored (PulseCommerce)

Marcus / Lauren —

We started seeing a major degradation in our checkout inference path at ~08:45 PDT. Key symptoms:
- 95th percentile tail latency jumped from ~80ms to ~1200ms across our critical route.
- Error rate (503) spiked to ~7% for the last 30 minutes.
- Committed reserved throughput (900 req/s) is only seeing ~420 req/s; requests are queuing at the client.

This is impacting live traffic and revenue. We previously signed a reserved capacity commitment (see attached DocuSign) and expect the committed throughput to be honored. We've attached error bundles and a set of throughput graphs.

Can we get an immediate triage and an exec-level bridge? If you can’t remediate quickly we need a clear fallback plan (failover to a shared fallback model or temporary capacity uplift). Please prioritize — our retention risk here is material.

Attachments: pulse_error_log_20280718.zip, throughput_graphs_19july.png

— Elena

Thanks for flagging, and sorry for the disruption. We're assembling a small bridge immediately. Short plan while we triage:
1) Scheduled 30-minute incident bridge at 10:00 PDT (join link: https://redwood.zoom.us/j/812345678).
2) Engineering will validate if the dedicated pool is hitting worker OOMs or throttles and, if needed, apply an emergency +30% temporary capacity uplift to your reserved pool.
3) Ops will enable a short-lived fallback routing to our shared low-latency pool for checkout traffic while we fix the dedicated pool.
4) I'll coordinate commercial remediation (credits / SLA exception) while we stabilize.

Aditya / Grace — can you confirm who owns the autoscaling policy on PulseCommerce's pool and whether there are known kernel/quantization regressions in the last deploy?

Elena — we will treat this as an exec-level incident and follow up with a 72-hour action plan and postmortem.

Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency + 503s — dedicated pool saturation (initial triage)

Quick triage notes (first 20m):
- Symptom: worker-side queueing + intermittent GPU OOM on pool worker group "pulse-2028-dedicated-a" after the 2028-07-18 runtime release. OOMs cause retries and queue backups -> 503s.
- Autoscaler: policy for this pool is configured with a conservative headroom (max 8 nodes). The recent traffic spike exceeded that cap; autoscaler did not provision additional nodes because the new runtime's memory footprint increased ~18%.
- Kernel/regression: we observed a memory allocation difference in the attention kernel shipped 2028-07-18; this increases KV cache memory. Root cause likely interaction of new kernel + model sequence length in your workload.

Immediate recommended actions (we can run these in parallel):
A) Emergency capacity uplift: +30% nodes to pulse-2028-dedicated-a (temporary, will revert after stabilization). Requires ops approval — Marcus, please confirm.
B) Short-term config: enable model fallback routing for checkout route to use redwood/gptq-3B-quant (smaller KV footprint) for up to 2 hours. Minimal quality loss empirically.
C) Hotfix deploy: rollback the attention kernel to 2028-07-15 build on the affected worker pool (causes 10–15 minute rolling restart).
D) Create incident ticket: SUP-4827 (tracking remediation, postmortem, and credit discussion).

I'll kick off (B) and open SUP-4827 immediately. If Marcus authorizes (A) I'll open a capacity request to ops to push the temporary nodes.

Attachments: proposed_runbook_patch.sh (snippet referenced)

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
SRE, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

We accept the temporary fallback to the quantized variant for checkout traffic if that reduces error rates. Please confirm expected client-side behavior (any schema or tokenization differences we need to handle). Also: timeline for the rollback vs capacity uplift? If rollback is 10–15 minutes but requires rolling restarts is that safe for our live traffic?

Two commercial asks while you triage:
- Please confirm that reserved throughput will be honored over the incident window or advise on how Redwood will compensate (we expect credits for lost committed throughput).
- We need an exec-level bridge recording (we will escalate internally if we don’t see timely resolution).

Quoted for context: "SUP-4827" was mentioned for tracking.

— Elena

Subject: Re: Production latency + 503s — reserved throughput remediation and next steps

Elena / Sanjay / Pulse team —

Status update following the bridge: we implemented the short-term fallback routing (redwood/gptq-3B-quant) at 10:09 PDT and observed error rates drop to <0.5% and 95p latency return to ~120ms within 7 minutes. Aditya rolled a kernel rollback candidate to one worker group and will proceed with a staged rollback across the fleet when overnight windows are confirmed.

Commercial commitments:
- We acknowledge the impact on committed throughput during the incident window. We will issue an interim credit for the hours where your effective throughput fell below the committed baseline (PULSE-9081 commercial team is copied). Detailed credit amount will be shared within 24 hours.
- We will produce a 72-hour action plan and a postmortem (SUP-4827) with remediation items: autoscaler headroom changes, runtime memory regression fix, and stronger rollout gating for attention kernels.

Immediate next steps for PulseCommerce (owner assignments):
- Marcus (Account): coordinate credit and contract amendment paperwork (DocuSign link: https://docusign.redwood.com/PULSE-9081-amend).
- Aditya (SRE): complete staged rollback and validate no regression for 48h.
- Grace (CS Ops): schedule a follow-up health check call in 48 hours and confirm SLOs.

We will treat this as highest priority. I’ll follow up with the formal 72-hour plan and a calendar invite for the postmortem. Thank you for the patience and immediate coordination.

— Marcus
